title: Shadow to Autonomy: 14-day bridge onboarding checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, actionable 14-day bridge for engineers who need a short, high-signal shadow period before autonomous ownership. Intended for ICs transferring between pods or newly hired engineers who completed the initial 7-day setup.

Goals (what success looks like by Day 14):
- Owner can triage and resolve standard production alerts in the on-call runbook without mentor step-in.
- Owner can own one small customer-facing change from design -> deploy -> postmortem.
- Manager and mentor agree on readiness using a 5-point rubric below.

Scope and assumptions:
- Not a replacement for full 90-day plan; this is a focused, execution-first bridge for continuity.
- Assumes access provisioning (git, infra, slack, CI) completed in week 0. If not, escalate to IT ticketing owner.

Primary stakeholders:
- New hire: (fill name)
- Mentor: (fill) - primary human check-ins, shadow signoff
- Manager: (fill) - final autonomy sign-off
- On-call buddy: (fill) - pairs for first 3 incidents

14-day schedule (high level):
- Day 0 (pre-bridge): confirm env access, add to on-call rotation doc, join team calendar and recurring standups.
- Days 1-3: Pair on triage. Mentor leads, new hire reads runbook aloud and performs guided steps. Objectives: runbook navigation, reproduce common failure locally or in staging.
  - Tasks: reproduce at least 1 incident in staging, open issue in minimal repro repo.
  - Notes: record command snippets in personal notes for quick reference.
- Days 4-7: Small ownership tasks. New hire picks a small bug or non-critical feature. Mentor reviews PRs but lets hire drive. Objectives: CI pipeline familiarity, PR checklist usage.
  - Tasks: link PR to JIRA, add reviewer tags, run CI and fix flakes.
- Days 8-11: Independent incident triage with mentor observation on-call. Mentor takes baton only for escalations. Objectives: deploy runbook steps without prompts.
  - Tasks: update runbook with any missing steps found.
- Days 12-14: Deliver a tiny customer-facing change (doc + code) and run a 30-minute retrospective with mentor. Manager gives final signoff using rubric.

Daily micro-checklist (copy into hire's doc):
- Morning: 15m sync with mentor (standups are insufficient).
- Before EOD: add 3 bullets to personal ramp-log: what I learned, what blocked me, who I pinged.
- Friday: short demo of week work (5–10m) in team retro.

Rubric for autonomy signoff (5-point scale, manager + mentor):
- Triage confidence (1=no exposure, 5=independent)
- Deploy ownership (1=never, 5=can run hotfixes + rollbacks)
- Code quality & PR hygiene (1=needs heavy edits, 5=clean + tests)
- Communication (1=need constant prompting, 5=proactive updates)
- Operational hygiene (1=not updating runbooks, 5=improves docs and shares learnings)

Scoring guidance: average score >= 4 => autonomy signoff. Any critical failure (score 1 on Triage or Deploy) => extend bridge by another week and repeat targeted tasks.

Templates & quick messages:
- Slack intro (to use on Day 0):
  "hi team — I’m (name), starting my bridge with (mentor). I’ll be focusing on owning alerts for the next two weeks. Ping me on threads or DM for pairing slots"
- PR description template (required for bridge work):
  - Summary, Customer impact, Test plan, Rollback plan, JIRA link, Screenshots/logs.

Common pitfalls / notes to mentor:
- Don’t over-protect: allow the hire to make low-risk mistakes; learning velocity matters more than superficial safety.
- Track the traction metric: number of independent triages per week. Target >=3 by week 2.
- If CI flakes repeatedly, schedule a 30m digging session and escalate flaky test ownership to infra team.

Artifacts to create/update during bridge:
- Personal ramp-log (daily bullets) — copy link to manager weekly.
- Small doc: "how I debug X service" (1–2 pages) and add to team knowledge base.
- One-line addition to runbook for any missing step.

Open questions / followups (notes):
- Should we auto-enroll hires into a 14-day pairing calendar? (Ops ticket: ONB-458)
- Add a low-friction checklist for mentors to certify signoff (checkboxes + short comments).

Signoff area (manager + mentor):
- Mentor name / date / quick note
- Manager name / date / hire readiness level

Appendix: quick checklist for mentors (copyable):
- Day 1: confirm access, add to on-call doc, share 'how to' snippets.
- Day 3: reproduce incident in staging.
- Day 7: review first PR and provide actionable feedback.
- Day 10: observe 2 independent triages.
- Day 14: run final 30m retro + complete rubric.

Last notes: treat this as a living template. People-ops will iterate based on feedback from mentors (Nadia/Priya collecting) — please add comments inline or ping #people-ops-onboarding-thread.
